title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.27095v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Language-model agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) face three runtime verification gaps: (i) action fabrication, where post-tool prose narrates side effects that failed, timed out, or never ran; (ii) provenance collapse, where unverified model prose or web text enters durable memory alongside executed tool outputs; and (iii) syndicated echo amplification, where mirrored web pages satisfy multi-source corroboration from one origin. Existing MCP firewalls inspect wire calls before execution, while LLM-judge guardrails require multi-gigabyte VRAM without binding prose to receipts. We present epistemic-guard (v0.5.2), an open-source Python library and out-of-process stdio MCP receipt proxy (15 modules, 0 MiB GPU VRAM). epistemic-guard isolates Ed25519 signing keys out of process, writes RFC 6962 Merkle logs with AER-1 receipt translation, checks post-turn prose on CPU with SHA-256-verified OpenVINO INT8 encoders (4 models, 279.48

translated_title: Epistemic Guard（认知守护）：面向工具使用型自主智能体的进程外MCP回执代理、回合后文本监督与来源门控记忆
translated_abstract: 使用模型上下文协议（MCP）的语言模型智能体面临三个运行时验证缺口：（i）动作伪造，即工具调用后的文本叙述了失败、超时或从未执行过的副作用；（ii）来源崩溃，即未经验证的模型文本或网页文本与已执行的工具输出一同进入持久化记忆；（iii）联合回声放大，即镜像网页从单一来源满足多来源交叉验证。现有的MCP防火墙在执行前检查线上调用，而LLM裁判类护栏需要数GB显存，且无法将文本叙述与回执绑定。我们提出了epistemic-guard（v0.5.2），一个开源Python库及进程外stdio MCP回执代理（15个模块，0 MiB GPU显存占用）。epistemic-guard将Ed25519签名密钥隔离在进程之外，写入带有AER-1回执翻译的RFC 6962 Merkle日志，并在CPU上使用经SHA-256验证的OpenVINO INT8编码器（4个模型，279.48（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出了开源库epistemic-guard，通过进程外MCP回执代理、回合后文本监督与来源门控记忆三大机制，在零GPU显存开销下解决工具使用型语言模型智能体的动作伪造、来源崩溃与回声放大三大运行时验证缺口。
en_tdlr: epistemic-guard is an open-source, zero-GPU-VRAM Python library that closes three runtime verification gaps in tool-using LLM agents—action fabrication, provenance collapse, and syndicated echo amplification—through out-of-process MCP receipt proxying, post-turn prose supervision, and provenance-gated memory.
